title: Issuing Standard for Workmanship Warranties Coverages and Certificates
content:
**Standard.** The Workmanship Warranties plan issued is the one the source work names as its warranty plan issued, issued on the delivery date of a repair order or the completion date of a glass job or calibration order, with the odometer at that date. Parts the customer supplied are excluded where the plan excludes customer-supplied parts, and sensors whose calibration the customer declined are excluded where the plan excludes declined calibrations; both exclusions are recorded on the coverage at issue. The certificate goes out by the plan's certificate delivery channel and is honored at any network center where the plan provides nationwide service. Coverage is never sold, extended or upgraded; a rework never starts a new term where the plan provides that a rework does not extend the term.

## What is recorded on a coverage at issue

| Item | Basis |
|---|---|
| Plan | The plan the source work names as its warranty plan issued |
| Issued date | The delivery date of a repair order, or the completion date of a glass job or calibration order |
| Odometer at issue | The odometer at the issued date |
| Customer-supplied parts | Whether the source work installed customer-supplied parts, recorded as an exclusion where the plan excludes them |
| Declined calibration | Whether a calibration on the source work was declined, recorded as an exclusion where the plan excludes declined calibrations |
| Owner on file | The customer who owns the vehicle at issue |

## Points of the standard

- **Dates by kind of source work.** A repair order, whether an insurance claim repair or a customer-pay repair, issues on its delivery date. A glass job or a calibration order issues on its completion date.
- **Certificate.** The certificate goes out by the plan's certificate delivery channel and is honored at any network center where the plan provides nationwide service.
- **No sale, extension or upgrade.** A coverage is never sold, extended or upgraded.
- **Rework and term.** Where the plan provides that a rework does not extend the term, a rework never starts a new term.

## Hypothetical example

A customer-pay repair is delivered on a hypothetical 4 May with the odometer at 31250 miles, and its source work names the Collision Lifetime Workmanship Warranty. The coverage is issued as a Collision Lifetime Workmanship Warranty dated 4 May with an odometer at issue of 31250 miles. Had the repair installed a part the customer supplied, that part would be recorded at issue as excluded wherever the plan excludes customer-supplied parts.
